files.lesson.md: --- order: 14 unit: transform node: AC9M7SP03 n3 title: Rotations summary: "A rotation turns a shape about a centre by an angle in a direction. About the origin, a quarter turn anticlockwise changes (x, y) to (−y, x) and a half turn changes it to (−x, −y)." language: maths voice: { name: af_heart, speed: 1.1 } hook: "The hands of a clock, a Ferris wheel, a spinning fan. Each turns about a centre by a certain angle, in a certain direction." connection: tile-rotation app: command: node "$REPO_ROOT/tools/serve.mjs" "$REPO_ROOT/dist/_playground-board" 8299 url: http://127.0.0.1:8299/index.html readySelector: "#gsum" layout: full explainPicture: { ref: turn.yml#explain-pic, caption: "A quarter turn anticlockwise about the origin: $(2, 1)$ becomes $(-1, 2)$." } explainClip: query: { code: "@turn.yml#explain", fresh: 1, id: explain } caption: "Turning about the origin" say: "Turn the triangle a quarter at a time." clip: - caption: { text: "A triangle, with the origin as the centre.", say: "A triangle, turning about the origin." } - wait: 800 - caption: { text: "A quarter turn anticlockwise.", say: "A quarter turn anticlockwise." } - click: Make the turn bigger - expect: { selector: "#gsum", contains: "Rotate 90°" } - wait: 1200 - caption: { text: "A half turn: both signs change.", say: "A half turn. Both signs change." } - click: Make the turn bigger - expect: { selector: "#gsum", contains: "Rotate 180°" } - wait: 1500 --- A **rotation** turns a shape about a fixed point, the **centre of rotation**. To describe one, give the **centre**, the **angle** and the **direction** (clockwise or anticlockwise). The shape keeps its size and shape. ## Predict: a quarter turn ```step stage: predict insight: "Committing to the image of a point after a quarter turn shows whether they swap coordinates or picture the turn." check: type: predict q: "Point A is at (2, 1). The triangle turns 90° anticlockwise about the origin. Where does A land?" options: ["(−1, 2)", "(1, 2)", "(−2, −1)", "(1, −2)"] actual: "(−1, 2). A is right of the centre, so it turns up and to the left. Its distance from the origin stays the same." ``` Picture a clock hand pointing right, turning up. ## Run: turn the triangle ```step stage: run insight: "Turning the triangle in quarter steps and reading the corners shows how each coordinate changes for 90°, 180° and 270°." try: { playground: board, starter: "turn.yml#run", height: 600 } check: { type: board, text: "Turn the triangle 90° anticlockwise. Was your prediction right?", when: "t = 90 and x(A) = -1 and y(A) = 2", explain: "A (2, 1) becomes A′ (−1, 2): the new x is the old y with its sign changed, and the new y is the old x." } ``` The black dot is the centre of rotation. The sliders turn the shape anticlockwise. About the origin, an anticlockwise turn of 90° changes $(x, y)$ to $(-y, x)$; 180° (a half turn) changes it to $(-x, -y)$; 270° changes it to $(y, -x)$. ## Investigate: how to turn a point ```step stage: investigate insight: "A quarter turn swaps and changes one sign, depending on the direction (Lee only swaps); a rotation needs a centre, an angle and a direction." tasks: - check: type: question q: "B is at (4, 1). It turns 180° about the origin. Where does B′ land?" options: ["(−4, −1)", "(4, −1)", "(−4, 1)", "(1, 4)"] answer: 0 feedback: [null, "That is a reflection in the x-axis.", "That is a reflection in the y-axis.", "That swaps the coordinates."] explain: "A half turn changes both signs: (−4, −1)." - check: type: bug code: "working.txt#lee" text: "Lee turns P (3, 1) by 90° anticlockwise about the origin. Click the line where his reasoning goes wrong." answer: 3 fault: logic misconception: rotate-swap-only explain: "Line 3: a quarter turn also changes a sign. P turns up and to the left, so the image is (−1, 3), not (1, 3)." - check: type: question q: "What three things do you need to describe a rotation?" options: ["The centre, the angle and the direction", "The angle only", "The axis and the angle", "The centre and the size of the shape"] answer: 0 feedback: [null, "Turning 90° about different centres gives different images.", "Axes belong to reflections.", "The size does not change in a rotation."] explain: "The same angle about a different centre, or in the other direction, gives a different image." ``` ### A half turn Both signs change. ### Find the mistake Read Lee's working. Which way does P turn? ### What describes a rotation ## Modify: change the turn and the centre ```step stage: modify insight: "Choosing an angle to reach a target, then moving the centre, shows the image depends on the centre; clockwise and anticlockwise turns are linked." try: { playground: board, starter: "turn.yml#free", height: 600 } tasks: - starter: "turn.yml#free" hint: ["A is at (2, 1).", "Three quarter turns anticlockwise is 270°."] check: { type: board, text: "Turn the triangle so that A′ lands at (1, −2).", when: "t = 270 and x(A) = 1 and y(A) = -2", explain: "A turn of 270° anticlockwise changes (2, 1) to (1, −2)." } - starter: "turn.yml#centre" hint: ["The centre is now (1, 0), not the origin.", "A is one right and one up from the centre. A quarter turn takes it to one left and one up."] check: { type: board, text: "The centre of rotation is (1, 0). Turn the triangle 90° anticlockwise. Where does A land?", when: "t = 90 and x(A) = 0 and y(A) = 1", explain: "A is (1, 1) from the centre; after a quarter turn it is (−1, 1) from the centre, which is (0, 1)." } - check: type: question q: "A turn of 90° clockwise ends in the same place as a turn of how many degrees anticlockwise?" options: ["270°", "90°", "180°", "360°"] answer: 0 feedback: [null, "Those are opposite directions.", "That is a half turn.", "That is back where it started."] explain: "A quarter turn clockwise is three quarter turns anticlockwise: 270°." - check: type: question q: "What does a rotation of 360° do?" options: ["Nothing: the shape ends up where it started", "Flips the shape", "Moves the shape one unit", "Doubles its size"] answer: 0 feedback: [null, "A flip is a reflection.", "A rotation about a centre does not slide.", "A rotation never changes the size."] explain: "A full turn brings every point back to where it started." ``` ### Three quarter turns ### A different centre ### Clockwise ### A full turn ## Practise: rotations ```step stage: practise insight: "Half turns, finding the turn between two points and a reflection review, mixed; swapping without a sign is the planted slip; the review keeps mirrors fresh." try: { playground: board, starter: "turn.yml#run", height: 600 } tasks: - check: type: answer q: "B is at (4, 1). After a 180° turn about the origin, what is the x-coordinate of B′?" answer: "-4" feedback: - ["4", "A half turn changes the sign of both coordinates."] explain: "x changes sign: −4. The image is (−4, −1)." - check: type: question q: "Which turn about the origin takes (2, 1) to (−1, 2)?" options: ["90° anticlockwise", "90° clockwise", "180°", "270° anticlockwise"] answer: 0 feedback: [null, "That would take (2, 1) to (1, −2).", "That would take it to (−2, −1).", "That would take it to (1, −2)."] explain: "(2, 1) to (−1, 2) is the rule (x, y) → (−y, x): a quarter turn anticlockwise." - check: type: answer q: "The point (3, 1) turns 90° anticlockwise about the origin. What is the y-coordinate of the image?" answer: "3" feedback: - ["1", "The new y is the old x."] explain: "(x, y) → (−y, x), so (3, 1) becomes (−1, 3)." - check: type: answer q: "Review: the point (3, 5) is reflected in the x-axis. What is the y-coordinate of the image?" answer: "-5" feedback: - ["5", "In the x-axis, y changes sign."] explain: "(3, 5) becomes (3, −5)." ``` ### A half turn ### Which turn ### A quarter turn ### Review: reflections ## Make: turn to a target ```step stage: make insight: "Finding the turn that puts a chosen corner on a target applies the rule and then states the full description: centre, angle and direction." try: { playground: board, starter: "turn.yml#free", height: 600 } hint: ["Corner B is at (4, 1).", "Try each turn and read B′."] check: { type: board, text: "Turn the triangle so that B′ is at (1, −4).", when: "x(B) = 1 and y(B) = -4", explain: "A turn of 270° anticlockwise about the origin changes (4, 1) to (1, −4)." } ``` Then describe the rotation fully: the centre, the angle and the direction. How else could you say it, turning clockwise? ## Make: a four-tile block, on paper ```step stage: make insight: "A four-tile block is one design turned a quarter turn at a time; each turn of 90° anticlockwise about the centre sends (x, y) to (−y, x)." hint: ["Turn once, write the new point, then turn that point again.", "A quarter turn anticlockwise sends (x, y) to (−y, x)."] check: type: reasoning paper: true q: "A four-tile block is made by turning one tile a quarter turn anticlockwise about the centre O (0, 0), again and again. A dot on the first tile is at (3, 1). Where is the dot on the third tile, after two quarter turns? Give its x-coordinate." steps: - ["One quarter turn anticlockwise: $(x, y)$ goes to $(-y, x)$", "the point turns about the centre $O$"] - ["$(3, 1)$ goes to $(-1, 3)$ on the second tile", "$x = 3$, $y = 1$, so $(-y, x) = (-1, 3)$"] - ["Turn again: $(-1, 3)$ goes to $(-3, -1)$ on the third tile", "$(-y, x)$ with $x = -1$ and $y = 3$"] - ["The x-coordinate is $-3$", "check: two quarter turns make a half turn, so $(3, 1)$ goes to $(-3, -1)$"] picks: - step: 2 q: "Where does (3, 1) go after one quarter turn anticlockwise?" options: - "(−1, 3)" - "(1, 3)" - "(3, −1)" answer: 0 feedback: [null, "That swaps the coordinates but forgets the sign change. It would be a reflection.", "That keeps x and changes the sign of y. It is a reflection, not a turn."] answer: "-3" tolerance: 0 feedback: - ["-1", "That is the point after one turn, (−1, 3). Turn once more."] - ["3", "Two quarter turns make a half turn, so both signs change."] criteria: - "I turned once and wrote the new point." - "I turned the new point again, not the original." - "I checked that two quarter turns make a half turn: (3, 1) to (−3, −1)." explain: "(3, 1) turns to (−1, 3), then to (−3, −1). The x-coordinate on the third tile is −3." ``` Do this one in your book, not on the screen. The tile and the dot are made up for the task. Sketch the centre and the dot, turn it once, then turn the new point again, and type the x-coordinate. **Also used in** - **Tiles and patterns.** Four-tile blocks and wallpaper repeat by turning one design a quarter turn at a time. - **Wheels and fans.** Ferris wheels and fans turn each part about a centre by the same angle. ```teacher summary: Students turn a shape about a centre and find the image of each corner for quarter and half turns (AC9M7SP03, node 3). time: 35 timing: Predict and Run 8 min · Investigate 8 min · Modify 10 min · Practise and Make 9 min goals: - I can rotate a shape 90°, 180° or 270° about the origin. - I can describe a rotation by its centre, angle and direction. - I can use the pattern in the coordinates to check an answer. struggle: Picturing the turn. Use tracing paper pinned at the centre, or have students point a pencil at the shape and turn it. before: > Do the Run board yourself first. Students need translations and reflections (previous lessons). The one idea: a rotation needs a centre, an angle and a direction. About the origin, an anticlockwise quarter turn is $(x, y) \to (-y, x)$; the half turn changes both signs. The common mistake is only swapping the coordinates (Lee's mistake). The board turns anticlockwise only; clockwise turns are the questions in Modify and Make (90° clockwise is 270° anticlockwise). Rotation is the hardest transformation to reason about: let students trace and turn before using the rule. The rule is a check on the answer, not the method. Turning about another centre (the second Modify task) is done by the picture: the rule does not apply. running: - "Predict: ask students to point a pencil and turn it a quarter." - "Run: ask what stays the same after each turn (the distance to the centre)." - "Investigate: ask how Lee could test his answer." - "Modify: for the centre (1, 0), ask where A is measured from." - "Make: ask for the description with the direction." - "Paper: the four-tile task is worked in books; the page marks the x-coordinate (-3) and the rule for one quarter turn. Books out, then look at the page for the second turn starting from the new point." stuck: - see: A student swaps the coordinates without a sign. ask: Which quadrant should the image be in? fix: Picture the turn first, then use the rule to check. - see: A student turns clockwise. ask: Which way do clock hands go? Which way do we turn here? fix: The board turns anticlockwise; clockwise 90° is 270° anticlockwise. - see: A student forgets the centre. ask: What point does the shape turn about? fix: Always name the centre, the angle and the direction. stretch: Show that reflecting in the x-axis and then the y-axis gives the same image as a 180° rotation about the origin. Which two reflections (one in the line y = x) make a 90° rotation? support: "Use tracing paper: trace the shape, pin the centre and turn the paper a quarter at a time." leads: > This completes AC9M7SP03. Where it leads: combining transformations and tessellations (Year 8); rotational symmetry. exit: q: The point (2, 3) turns 180° about the origin. Where is the image? a: "(−2, −3): both signs change." explain: > A **rotation** turns a shape about a **centre** by an **angle** in a **direction** (clockwise or anticlockwise). The shape keeps its size. About the origin, anticlockwise: 90° changes $(x, y)$ to $(-y, x)$; 180° changes it to $(-x, -y)$; 270° changes it to $(y, -x)$. ```

files.working.txt:
# Lee's working for the "find the mistake" task. Plain text: students click the wrong line, nothing runs.

# region: lee
The point P is (3, 1). Lee turns it 90° anticlockwise about the origin.
A quarter turn is a big move, so P goes round to the next quadrant.
A quarter turn just swaps the coordinates.
So the image of P is (1, 3).
# endregion
